The second stage is the one most executives picture when they hear that AI is failing. S&P Global reports that firms abandoned, on average, forty-six per cent of projects between proof of concept and adoption. The share of companies abandoning most of their initiatives rose from seventeen to forty-two per cent in a year. NANDA's funnel showed a comparable drop from pilot to production.

Two cautions. S&P has not published its field dates or question wording. And a rising abandonment rate partly reflects a larger stock of projects available to abandon. The direction is consistent across sources.
